channel.title: The Grant Desk - Grants, AI, Tech & Research, US, weekly digest
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Grants, AI, Tech & Research, US, weekly digest. Released weekly: each Sunday's drop carries one entry per grant added in the week before it (Sunday to Saturday). A call that closes before its drop goes out is not sent; the website lists those.

item.title: Sundance Episodic Lab 2027: Alfred P. Sloan Grant Track (science and technology series) (closes 3 Dec)
item.description:
Sundance Institute with the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation
Deadline: 3 Dec 2026
Award: USD 17,000 grant plus creative support through the Episodic Lab. Submission fee waived with code EpSloanGrantX121426 on FilmFreeway.

An extended Sloan-only round of the Sundance Episodic Lab for original half-hour or one-hour series whose subject is science, technology or mathematics, or a scientist, engineer or mathematician. Open to a writer or a two-person writing team.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: GLEAM 2027: Request for Light-Based Artwork Proposals (Olbrich Botanical Gardens; honorariums USD 5,000 to 30,000) (closes 6 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Olbrich Botanical Gardens (City of Madison Parks Division and Olbrich Botanical Society)
Deadline: 6 Jan 2027, 23:59 CST
Award: All-inclusive honorarium of USD 5,000 to 30,000 per artwork, covering artist fee, materials, fabrication, travel, lodging, install and maintenance. Usually only one USD 30,000 project is selected; proposals under USD 25,000 get the most consideration. Free host lodging and loan projectors and speakers are available. No application fee stated.

GLEAM is an annual night-time light art exhibition across a 16-acre botanical garden and a 10,000 sq ft tropical conservatory.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: NYSCA/Wave Farm Media Arts Assistance Fund (MAAF) for Artists 2027 (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Wave Farm (NYSCA regrant)
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027, 23:59 EST
Award: Up to USD 7,500. No application fee.

A NYSCA regrant run by Wave Farm supporting New York State artists to complete or present new sound and moving-image works, including work with emergent technologies.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Awesome Foundation Local Chapters: USD 1,000 Monthly Micro-grants (US, UK, Canada, Australia, NL, Asia) (rolling)
item.description:
Awesome Foundation (local chapters)
Deadline: Rolling, apply any time
Award: Usually USD 1,000 (or local equivalent) per grant, no strings attached, typically one grant per chapter per month. No application fee.

The Awesome Foundation is a network of volunteer giving circles: in each chapter about ten trustees pool their own money to give a USD 1,000 no-strings micro-grant, usually monthly, to a project that adds "awesome" to their area: art, public interventions, community tech, events, science and civic...

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: University of Notre Dame: Love Ethic Social Innovator Fellowships 2028 (residency plus USD 15,000 and up to USD 50,000 project funding) (closes 11 Dec)
item.description:
University of Notre Dame, Institute for Ethics and the Common Good
Deadline: 11 Dec 2026
Award: Stipend for housing during the residency plus relocation support; USD 15,000 to the fellow's organisation to offset the four-week sabbatical; up to USD 50,000 in subgrant funding after the residency to pilot the proposed project; travel to all programme gatherings covered. No application fee.

Up to six short-term fellowships for practitioners outside academia (nonprofit leaders, community organisers, social workers, faith leaders, entrepreneurs, public-sector professionals) who want time and space to design a new initiative grounded in love-based ethics.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Craigardan Trillium Fellowship 2027 (residency for artists, activists and scholars of color, USD 4,600 + USD 500 honorarium) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Craigardan
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: USD 4,600 fellowship toward a minimum two-week residency (covers the residency fee), plus a USD 500 honorarium. Travel, materials and personal expenses are not covered. USD 25 application fee (waivers available on request).

The Trillium Fellowship supports artists, activists and scholars of color working in any discipline who would benefit from the time and space to pursue their work or find creative retreat at Craigardan, a residency and farm in the Adirondacks.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Kala Art Institute: Media Arts Fellowship 2027-28 (Berkeley; USD 3,000 stipend) (closes 1 Mar 2027)
item.description:
Kala Art Institute
Deadline: 1 Mar 2027
Award: USD 3,000 stipend plus facility access.

Kala's long-running Media Arts Fellowship supports four artists working in film and video, sound, animation, performance cinema and media installation. ELIGIBILITY: local, national and international artists not enrolled in a degree programme.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Folger Institute Artistic Research Fellowships 2027-28 (USD 4,000 to 5,000 per month) (closes 15 Jan 2027)
item.description:
Folger Shakespeare Library (Folger Institute)
Deadline: 15 Jan 2027, 23:59 EST
Award: USD 4,000 per virtual month or USD 5,000 per onsite month.

Artistic research fellowships for artists whose work needs primary research on the early modern world (about 1400 to 1800) and its legacies, using the Folger's collections. ELIGIBILITY: any artist; no degree required and no citizenship rule stated.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Spencer Education Journalism Fellowship 2027-28 (Columbia Journalism School) (closes 4 Feb 2027)
item.description:
Spencer Fellowship at Columbia Journalism School
Deadline: 4 Feb 2027
Award: Residential stipend USD 85,000 or non-residential stipend USD 43,000, plus a USD 7,500 travel and research budget. Non-residential fellows also get airfare and hotel for required NYC trips. No application fee.

The Spencer Education Journalism Fellowship, based at Columbia Journalism School, supports ambitious, research-savvy storytellers producing books, magazine features, documentaries and podcasts that deepen public understanding of critical issues in education.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Jane Street Graduate Research Fellowship 2027 (tuition plus USD 50,000 stipend) (closes 13 Nov)
item.description:
Jane Street
Deadline: 13 Nov 2026
Award: Full tuition and fees for the award year plus a USD 50,000 stipend (or local-currency equivalent; taxable). Finalists receive USD 5,000. No application fee.

Jane Street's Graduate Research Fellowship supports exceptional doctoral students in electrical engineering and computer science, mathematics, physics or statistics; research does not need to relate to trading.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network (AIAI): Seed Grants 2026 for humanities-forward AI research in Atlanta (closes 15 Nov)
item.description:
Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network (AIAI), Mellon Foundation funded
Deadline: 15 Nov 2026
Award: Up to USD 5,000 per project. In line with Mellon policy, no institutional overhead may be charged. Individuals taking the award outside an institution or employer pay income tax on it. No application fee.

AIAI funds humanities-forward AI research and community building that takes place in, or is focused on, the city of Atlanta. 2026 RESEARCH AREAS: Data Centers; AI Civics; AI Literacies; AI and Archives; Small Language Models; Capitalism, Anticapitalism, and Critique.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: Van Alen Institute: Re:Paris Prize, USD 35,000 travel research fellowship on design in Africa and its diaspora (US-based applicants) (closes 22 Nov)
item.description:
Van Alen Institute
Deadline: 22 Nov 2026
Award: USD 35,000 travel fellowship; one US-based winner selected through this open call (two Africa-based winners were selected via the 2026 Pan-African Biennale).

The Re:Paris Prize, run by Van Alen Institute, funds research into how design plays a transformative role in Africa and its diaspora. Each winner receives a USD 35,000 travel fellowship for field research that requires international travel to connect with experts and opportunities.

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: IHS AI and the Workforce Research Grants (up to USD 20,000) (closes 15 Dec)
item.description:
Institute for Humane Studies (IHS)
Deadline: 15 Dec 2026
Award: Up to USD 20,000 per award; larger awards possible for exceptional projects. Covers research costs (research assistants, datasets, LLM subscriptions, travel to present), not salary or overhead.

Research grants for academic scholars studying how AI is changing jobs, productivity and economic opportunity. Economics-leaning; IHS is a libertarian-leaning institute. Funds direct research costs only. No country restriction stated. Deadline 15 December 2026 (no time zone given).

Apply on the organiser's site

item.title: City of Palo Alto Code:ART 2027: Interactive Media Installations (up to USD 9,000 each)
item.description: City of Palo Alto Public Art Program · deadline 16 Nov 2026 · Up to USD 9,000 per installation, for up to five installations. No application fee.

item.title: City of Palo Alto Code:ART 2027: Lytton Plaza Installation Commission (USD 20,000)
item.description: City of Palo Alto Public Art Program · deadline 16 Nov 2026 · USD 20,000 commission budget. No application fee.

item.title: Burning Man: BRC Honoraria Art Grants 2027 (Letter of Intent)
item.description: Burning Man Project · deadline 29 Oct 2026 · USD 1.5 million annual art-grant budget across approximately 75 projects; grants fund 40 to 60% of the proposed total budget, and the official page notes grants over USD 20,000 are rare. No fixed per-award figure is published. No application fee.

item.title: Beam Center: 2027 Beam Camp Project Open Call (USD 5,000 commission, remote-friendly)
item.description: Beam Center · deadline 30 Nov 2026 · USD 5,000 award to the selected proposer, plus a fabrication budget of approximately USD 15,000. No application fee.

item.title: Anthropic Economic Futures Research Fund (research grants on AI's economic impacts)
item.description: Anthropic · deadline Rolling / undated · USD 200 million committed overall. Grants primarily in the USD 5-30 million range per project, with a USD 1 million minimum and flexibility upward for well-scoped, high-potential-impact projects. The separate small-grant Research Awards tier (USD 10,000-50,000 plus USD 5,000 in Claude API credits) is currently paused. No application fee.
